basis: Vertebral segmentation defects define this skeletal dysplasia; hemivertebrae in 2/2 reported patients.
Inherited PRNP-associated spongiform neurodegeneration; dementia in 9/9. Neuropsychiatric features reflect brain disease.
Congenital anomalous systemic venous drainage; hypoxemia does not establish pulmonary damage, and brain abscess is a minority complication.
Inherited cerebral vascular amyloid deposition with neurodegeneration; cataracts 30-79%. Hearing impairment also 30-79%, omitted because of the four-axis cap.
Motor neuron degeneration and dementia define the disease; ophthalmoplegia reflects neurologic dysfunction rather than intrinsic eye damage.
CD81 antibody deficiency; immune-complex renal injury with renal failure and autoimmune thrombocytopenia each reported in 1/1 patient. Hepatomegaly alone is insufficient.
Benign neoplasm arising in the fallopian tube, a reproductive organ outside the axes.
Microcephaly and epilepsy establish neurologic disease; micropenis alone does not establish endocrine dysfunction.
Central movement disorder with dystonia and choreoathetosis; abnormal movements do not establish skeletal muscle damage.
Tumour arises in the peritoneal lining of the abdominal cavity, assigned to the gastrointestinal axis.
Umbrella group of hereditary reticulate skin pigmentation disorders; no shared extracutaneous damage established.
Skeletal dysplasia, progressive retinal/myopic and cataract disease, and conductive deafness define this subtype.
Carcinoma originates in vulvar sweat glands, which are skin appendages.
Defining cleft palate and blepharophimosis affect mouth and eyelids; frequent male hypospadias is a urethral malformation. Intellectual disability is only 5-29%.
Progressive inherited macular and retinal degeneration with impaired colour, night and peripheral vision.
Acquired peripheral nerve disease; additional organs depend on the specific underlying subtype.
Structural and functional disease of the soft palate and pharyngeal closure; associated hearing impairment occurs in 30-79%.
Stapes ankylosis and bilateral conductive hearing loss occur in 80-99%; middle-ear ossicular disease stays within the ear axis.
Bone fragility, joint hypermobility and abnormal skin define the overlap syndrome. Blue sclerae do not establish eye damage; arterial rupture occurs in 1/5.
Acrofacial skeletal dysplasia; oligodontia occurs in 80-99% and sparse hair in 30-79%. Ear position and facial appearance do not establish sensory damage.
Skeletal dysplasia with core dysautonomia/sensory loss; respiratory insufficiency 6/6 and visual dysfunction 80-99%. Dental and hair abnormalities omitted by cap.
Inherited cerebral amyloid angiopathy with neurodegeneration; early cataracts are near-universal. Progressive deafness is also common, omitted by the four-axis cap.
Developmental delay/intellectual disability and syndromic obesity define the condition; obesity occurs in 30-79%. Specific ocular abnormalities are only 5-29%.
Constitutional trisomy 8 commonly causes skeletal/joint abnormalities and developmental impairment; renal malformations occur in roughly 30-50%. Malignancy risk is excluded.
Mitochondrial respiratory-chain defect causing hypoglycemia and lactic acidosis; hepatomegaly with raised ALT/AST supports hepatic injury in the reported patient (1/1).
